campaign: MOSS in overgo does what the MOSS Ultra workflow does in ComfyUI, each section held to ComfyUI's recording

items.title: An operation that fails before recording its run names its cause beside the run it lacks, so the Library's failed validation in the model-journey lane says why

steps.title: The Library's validation of the hub model completes as the model-journey lane drives it, its cause, which failure-cause/do names, found by reproducing it and cured
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-17: failure-cause/do makes the model journey's failure say why; the break itself stays. The Library's validation of the hub model (Qwen2.5-0.5B, libraryintake validate: an exact suite recorded and replayed on the card, its verification published and the capability activated) returned an error before it published its run, and its cause was hidden behind the run it lacked. With failure-cause/do the journey's failure names it; the step reproduces the validation as the journey drives it, finds where it fails among the commits since 8dfa48064, where the lane last passed, and cures it, the journey's validation completing again.

Serves: a working model's Library validation, the model-journey lane.

Check: TestModelJourneyLibraryValidation, in the model-journey lane's environment, on the card.

Batch: device lane.

items.title: MOSS's three Turbo sections, 8 steps at guidance 1 through the adapters each stacks, are held to the workflow's Turbo recordings as its sections of 50 steps are

steps.title: MOSS's three Turbo sections, 8 steps at guidance 1 through the adapters each stacks, are held to the workflow's Turbo recordings as its sections of 50 steps are
steps.rationale:
Note: The owner's note of 2026-11-17: moss-eight-step comes before the 3-megapixel speed work, since three of the MOSS Ultra workflow's six sections are Turbo, none held to its recording yet, and 8 steps is the workflow's own fast path. moss-ultra-compare gave each Turbo section a preset (section-presets: 8 steps at guidance 1 on ER-SDE and bong_tangent, DMD2 and the SFT adapter stacked at 1, moss-control before them for depth, image to image Turbo at denoise 0.72) and the adapters' stacking (stacked-adapters), and the recorder kept each Turbo section's final latent and finished picture (fixtures/comfy/moss-ultra/recordings/pass-1). Each is asked as its recording asks it (its loader's adapters at their strengths, its sharpening, its picture, the depth section's control over the first half of the sampling with no block skipped and its map made as the section makes it) on the workflow's own files, and held to floors of agreement with ComfyUI's set from its first measured run less 3 dB, its input changed (reseeded, or its picture mirrored) keeping the latent below, as golden-floor holds the sections of 50 steps; the floor test's loop is shared. Its check sits beside those floors in internal/latentimage, whose recordings and model root it reads, in place of the adaptiveparity test the step was filed with.

Serves: done = each of the six sections agrees with its ComfyUI recording.

Check: TestTheTurboSectionsHoldTheirGoldenFloors, on the card.

Batch: device lane.

items.title: Where a MOSS step's time goes at 2368 x 1344, against ComfyUI's 1.1 s, and the depth estimate's 80 s on the processor, is measured part by part, the largest share cured after

steps.title: Where a MOSS step's time goes at 2368 x 1344, against ComfyUI's 1.1 s, and the depth estimate's 80 s on the processor, is measured part by part, the largest share cured after
steps.rationale:
Note: The owner's note of 2026-11-17: speed is the largest gap left. At the sections' own size, 2368 x 1344, a MOSS step takes 6.1 s in overgo and 1.1 s in ComfyUI (golden-floor's own-size reading, finding evidence:sha256:b277875b), and a depth section's Depth Anything V2 Small estimate takes 80 s on the processor for a 1024 x 576 picture, 0.35 s of it loading (finding evidence:sha256:9f5331e7). Speed work first finds where the time goes (lessons: a part judged slow is compared with the reference engine's same phase on the same input), so this step times one step at 2368 x 1344 part by part (the denoiser's blocks by kind: attention, feed-forward, the adapters' branches, guidance's passes; the host's share between launches) and the depth estimate by its encoder blocks and its head, and holds that the parts account for the whole. The cure of the largest share is filed from what it shows.

Serves: the six sections at their own size, and the depth sections' runs and previews.

Check: TestWhereAMossStepsTimeGoes, on the card.

Batch: device lane.

items.title: Text to image and prompt mode 3 are held to ComfyUI on a real prompt and a filled builder, their floors set from recordings of them, and image to image at denoise 1, the same run as text to image, goes

steps.title: Text to image and prompt mode 3 are held to ComfyUI on a real prompt and a filled builder, their floors set from recordings of them, and image to image at denoise 1, the same run as text to image, goes
steps.rationale:
Note: The owner's note of 2026-11-17: text to image and prompt mode 3 were recorded on the workflow's empty prompt and an empty builder, so their floors (golden-floor: 1.55 dB on latents, 15.11 dB on pictures for text to image; 0.88 and 16.50 for mode 3) show only that overgo's draw is closer to ComfyUI's than another seed's is, the chaotic sensitivity an empty prompt has (overgo against its own 8-bit attention: 2.38 dB). Both sections are recorded again with a real prompt, and mode 3 with the builder's fields and regions filled (comfy-reference -record with -set on the prompt node and the builder's inputs), twice each as pass-1 and pass-2 were, and their floors are set from those recordings by the golden-floor method (the first reading less 3 dB, beside a reseeded control). Image to image at denoise 1 starts from the noise alone, the same run as text to image, so its case goes.

Note: 2026-11-17, SQA-410 folded in (the owner's note): the floors' comparison scores pictures and latents it should refuse. squareColourMeans drops a picture's partial 8-pixel squares and pictureDecibels checks only that the two lists of means are as long, so a picture a column wider agrees at +Inf dB; decibelsOverSquares answers -Inf on lists of different lengths and NaN from a NaN sample; and each negative control (the reseeded and mirrored draws) is held only to scoring under its floor, so an invalid comparison passes it. The comparison refuses two pictures of different sizes, latents of different lengths, and any non-finite number, before it scores them, and a control counts only as a valid comparison scoring under the floor (golden_floor, image_to_image and depth_control model tests).

Serves: done = each section and prompt mode agrees with its ComfyUI recording, on prompts that say something.

Check: TestUltraSectionsHoldTheirGoldenFloors, on the card, with ComfyUI's recordings.

Batch: device lane.

items.title: The cycle's lanes and a commit take turns at the machine, a ready commit first, so neither stops the other

steps.title: The cycle's lanes and a commit take turns at the machine, a ready commit first, so neither stops the other
steps.rationale:
Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-17: the cycle's lanes and a commit could not run together. Checked: a commit's test stage holds at most the machine's commit free as it starts (processcontrol jobBound: need + free), and with the lanes' model tests holding the rest, moss-speed/attention's commit was refused at 18.3 GiB ("the tree reached its memory limit ... the commit free at its start"); the audio lane's test process died out of memory (VirtualAlloc errno 1455) while other work shared the machine; and four finished steps waited the lanes' hours. The two take turns at the machine: the lanes run takes a turn for each package it runs and gives it up between packages, a commit takes the same turn for its stages, and a commit waiting is served first (processcontrol TurnWaited tells a holder another waits), so the lanes yield between packages to a ready commit and resume after it, neither refused for the other's memory and neither stopped.

Serves: every commit while the lanes run, and lanes-on-close, which starts lanes beside the work of the next row.

Check: TestTheLanesGiveTheirTurnToAReadyCommit, host only.

Batch: host lane.

items.title: A row's closing commit runs the cycle's lanes at that commit, with no timer, so a break in a working model is found beside the commit that caused it

steps.title: A row's closing commit runs the cycle's lanes at that commit, with no timer, so a break in a working model is found beside the commit that caused it
steps.rationale:
Note: The owner's review of 2026-11-17: two of the cycle's five lanes failed at 1ab2ac601, 66 commits after their last run (8dfa48064, 2026-11-16), so a break in a working model was found a day from the commit that caused it: the oscillator clip asked at scale 0 since preset-form/do (clip-scale), and the Library's validation (failure-cause). Nothing ran the lanes between: a cycle runs them only when the plan is empty (HandStartDue), and a timer would guess a cadence. A row's closing commit, the landing that completes its last open step, starts the cycle's lanes at that commit, from a checkout of it so the working folder stays free (as the owner's note asked), taking turns with commits (lanes-turns), its record kept where the lanes' is (lane_runs.json); a run already going at an older commit is overtaken by the next close, not stacked.

Serves: a working model's break found beside the row that broke it.

Check: TestARowsClosingRunsTheLanesAtItsCommit, host only.

Batch: host lane.

items.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test

steps.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test
steps.rationale:
The evidence: cuda-synthetic/tag moved every untagged CUDA test that reads the data root behind modeltest but one. TestSenseNovaVariableRequestResources runs SenseNova's 8B production generation in an isolated measurement process, and docs/image_video_capacity.json names its retained measurement by the bytes of its file (evidence:sha256:888854b5...), which the store holds; tagged, its bytes changed and TestImageVideoCapacityAcceptance found no evidence under the new identity. A measurement is taken again only on a card to itself, and the readings campaign holds the card until its Wan arms are drawn, so the file stays in the gate, named by the check as measuredInPlace, and this row follows the campaign.

The change: the test carries //go:build modeltest, it is measured again on a quiet card into the store, the capacity record and its protocol digest (imageVideoCapacitySHA256) name the new identity, and measuredInPlace goes, so internal/sensenovarecipe leaves the cuda lane.

Check: a whole-tree test with measuredInPlace gone, named afresh so it fails before the change: TestTheGateRunsNoRealModelTest.

Refiled 2026-11-16 from cuda-resources/do, whose step carried no card need, so dispatch gave it while the readings campaign held the card: this step carries -needs-card and waits for a card to itself.

items.title: A picture request naming an adapter is bound to the adapter's bytes, so a replaced adapter is read again and never replayed

steps.title: A picture request naming an adapter is bound to the adapter's bytes, so a replaced adapter is read again and never replayed
steps.rationale:
Note: SQA-406 (P2): a picture request naming an adapter (<model>/adapters/<name>.safetensors) keys its run by the recipe, the request's JSON and the code (capabilityruntime RunKeyOf), and the HF pipeline's inventory (modelartifact fromHFPipeline) holds model_index's components alone, so the adapters directory is outside the model's identity: a replaced adapter file under the same name replays the earlier run's picture before media_adapter reads the new weights. The cure binds the named adapter's content to the request where the image source resolves it, so a changed adapter is a new run and an unchanged one keeps its resident weights across strengths; the artifact, replay and resident-session owners stay as they are. The check serves a fixed-seed request naming an adapter, replaces the adapter's bytes under its name, and wants the second request computed afresh (its run key differs), and the same bytes again to replay.

Serves: SQA-406, a served picture that follows its adapter's bytes.

Batch: host lane.

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
